title: Dzao Min language - Wikipedia
text: Dzao Min is a Hmong–Mien language of China. Mao reports a total of more than 60,000 speakers in Liannan County and Yangshan County of Guangdong, and in Yizhang County of Hunan. The speakers from Bapai, Guangdong are also called Bapai Yao.

title: Ethnic origin of Hmong-Mien
text: The origin of the Hmong-Mien is closely linked to the origin of the Han Chinese as both tribes have been living in adjacent regions since 3000 BC. Hmong-Mien are called Miao-Yao (苗瑤) aka San Miao (三苗) in China.

title: Iu Mien language
text: The Iu Mien language, spoken by the Yao (Mien) peoples, traces its origins to southern China, with migrations beginning around the 2nd millennium BCE as proto-Hmong-Mien speakers dispersed southward under pressure from expanding Han Chinese populations.
